A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BMC research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison, including matching content across pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original error-diagnosis, adaptive-sampling and reinforcement-learning experiments, alongside ablations and geometric analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds programming-task evaluations, additional model evaluations and score-correlation results.

M1.justification: Appendix D.3 introduces a code-specific BMC instantiation using AST Jaccard similarity and token-substitution rates without terminal-answer tokens. This changes the verification scoring for programming tasks; the original six-component estimator, reconstruction procedure, rejection sampling and alignment objective remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds actual evaluations on HumanEval and MBPP in Appendix D.3. This substantially extends coverage from mathematical and scientific question answering to open-ended program generation, while retaining GSM8K, MATH, ARC-C and GPQA.

E2.justification: Table 8 extends the existing error-diagnosis comparator set—Model Confidence, Self-Consistency and Self-Evaluation—to programming tasks. Existing comparisons retain their methods. Table 9 evaluates BMC on additional backbones rather than introducing competing verification methods.

E3.justification: Appendix D.4 adds GSM8K evaluations with LLaDA-MoE-7B-A1B-Instruct, using 1B active parameters, and the 16B dense LLaDA2.1-mini. The new correlation analysis specifies LLaDA-8B-Instruct and per-dataset sample counts. Previously stated masking, reconstruction, sampling and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds an analysis asking whether BMC scores track Model Confidence, reporting correlations across four benchmarks in Table 10. Appendix D.4 also tests consistency across model architectures and scales. Existing component ablations, sensitivity studies, geometric validation and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: v1 already reports Spearman correlations with p-values and a chi-square test in Appendix E.1. Table 10 extends the existing correlation/significance reporting practice to another relationship. Neither version adds or revises repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their results, but Tables 8–10 substantially extend the evidence with programming-task discrimination, additional-backbone performance and score-confidence associations. New BMC AUROCs are 0.687 on HumanEval, 0.662 on MBPP, and 0.858/0.853 on GSM8K with the two added backbones. Table 10 reports correlations ranging from 0.079 to 0.301. These are additional results, not same-setting improvements over v1. On MBPP, BMC AUPR is 0.668 versus Self-Consistency's 0.669.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, propositions, assumptions, equations and proofs are retained. Appendix A adds a note describing the propositions as conditional motivation rather than deployment guarantees, but does not revise their mathematical statements or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about geometric verification, diagnosis, adaptive inference and alignment. The added experiments support existing generality claims without redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 newly emphasizes domain-specific dissimilarity design, and Appendix A qualifies the theory's applicability to deployed models. Added passages interpret programming and architecture results as generalization evidence, and low score-confidence correlations as evidence of distinct dynamics. Stronger guarantee language elsewhere remains unchanged.

D1.justification: The additions identify code-scoring ingredients and the extra model checkpoints with their total/active parameter configurations. This provides limited new technical information. Appendix C remains unchanged, and the code experiments lack details such as the backbone, AST construction and score aggregation.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and related-work positioning remain unchanged. The title of Tsui's Self-Correction Bench reference is corrected, but its author, year and arXiv identifier establish that it is the same cited work.

P1.justification: v3 adds a short methodological clarification, a theory qualification, two appendix subsections and a correlation-analysis paragraph. Affiliations, publication information, the appendix contents and one reference title are updated. Most prose and the overall organization are retained.

P2.justification: Three appendix tables are added for programming results, model architectures and correlations. Caption formatting, spacing and page flow change, including relocation of later qualitative figures. All seven original figures and their substantive visual content are retained.

improvement.justification: The added programming and architecture evaluations broaden empirical support, while the Appendix A note better qualifies the theory. The gains are limited by sparse code-experiment documentation and overstated interpretations: Table 8 does not support consistent superiority on MBPP AUPR, and Table 10's low correlations do not establish entirely distinct mechanisms. Stronger theoretical-guarantee language also remains elsewhere. These additions provide a modest net improvement without resolving the central limitations.
